caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular woven textile, primarily composed of dark blue, red, and white colors. The textile features a repeating geometric pattern that includes large red square-like motifs with cross shapes intersecting at the center, set against a dark blue background. Smaller diamond and checkerboard patterns, primarily in white and occasionally with red, are interspersed between these larger motifs. White vertical stripes run through the motifs, creating a column-like effect, and there are sections with a grid of short parallel bars in both white and red. Along the bottom and right edges, the textile terminates in twisted fringes of blue, red, and white threads. In the lower right-hand corner, a small triangular section of the textile is turned up, revealing the reverse side, which displays the same geometric pattern but with colors inverted or rearranged. The background of the image is a plain, off-white surface with some smudges and signs of wear.
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
